---- MODULE W4Od1m7p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxVer, NoOne

ASSUME NoOne \notin Controllers

VARIABLES ver, owner, inflight, pending, applied, acked

vars == <<ver, owner, inflight, pending, applied, acked>>

Messages == [ctrl: Controllers, expVer: 0..MaxVer]

Init ==
  /\ ver = 0
  /\ owner = NoOne
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ pending = Controllers
  /\ applied = {}
  /\ acked = {}

\* A controller reads the current version and issues a CAS request; because
\* inflight is a set (not a queue), any such message may be delivered and
\* processed at any later point, modeling arbitrary network reordering.
Send(c) ==
  /\ c \in pending
  /\ ~ \E m \in inflight : m.ctrl = c
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[ctrl |-> c, expVer |-> ver]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, pending, applied, acked>>

SendAny == \E c \in Controllers : Send(c)

\* The CAS succeeds only when the message's expected version still matches
\* the live record; this equality guard is what prevents a reordered, stale
\* write from clobbering an update that has already been accepted.
Apply(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.expVer = ver
  /\ ver' = ver + 1
  /\ owner' = m.ctrl
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ applied' = applied \cup {m.ctrl}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {m.ctrl}
  /\ UNCHANGED acked

ApplyAny == \E m \in inflight : Apply(m)

\* A message whose expected version no longer matches the record is a stale
\* reordered CAS attempt; it is rejected/discarded and its controller keeps
\* retrying (remains pending) instead of overwriting the record.
Reject(m) ==
  /\ m \in inflight
  /\ m.expVer # ver
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, pending, applied, acked>>

RejectAny == \E m \in inflight : Reject(m)

\* Once a controller's write has been accepted it is told so, and it stops
\* treating its runway-slot request as outstanding.
Ack(c) ==
  /\ c \in applied
  /\ c \notin acked
  /\ acked' = acked \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, owner, inflight, pending, applied>>

AckAny == \E c \in Controllers : Ack(c)

Next == SendAny \/ ApplyAny \/ RejectAny \/ AckAny

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
           /\ WF_vars(SendAny) /\ WF_vars(ApplyAny)
           /\ WF_vars(RejectAny) /\ WF_vars(AckAny)

\* Safety: an already-accepted controller is never forgotten back into
\* "pending", and the record's owner is always someone whose write really
\* was accepted -- captures "no lost updates to the shared record".
NoLostUpdate ==
  /\ \A c \in Controllers : c \in applied => c \notin pending
  /\ owner # NoOne => owner \in applied

\* Liveness: despite reordering and rejection of stale CAS messages, every
\* controller's runway-slot update is eventually applied and acknowledged.
EventualDelivery == <>(acked = Controllers)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    c1 = c1
    c2 = c2
    NoOne = NoOne
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    MaxVer = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
PROPERTY EventualDelivery
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator keeps a single shared runway-slot-assignment
record guarded by a compare-and-swap (CAS) register: the record carries a
version number, and a controller may only overwrite it by presenting the
version it last observed. Controllers read the current version, then send a
CAS request message; because the network can reorder messages, a request
built against an old version may be delivered and processed long after a
newer version has already been installed by someone else. The CAS discipline
means such a stale request is rejected rather than silently clobbering the
record, and the rejected controller retries against the fresh version until
its assignment is accepted and acknowledged.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A controller whose runway-slot update has already been
accepted is never left marked pending again, and the record's current owner
is always a controller whose write was genuinely accepted -- no accepted
update is ever silently lost or overwritten by a stale, reordered request.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Despite arbitrary reordering and rejection of stale CAS
messages, every controller's runway-slot update is eventually applied and
acknowledged.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Node

None == "None"

Quorum == (Cardinality(Node) \div 2) + 1

VARIABLES requested, voteMsgs, granted, active, votesSeen

vars == <<requested, voteMsgs, granted, active, votesSeen>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ requested \subseteq Node
  /\ voteMsgs \subseteq (Node \X Node)
  /\ granted \in [Node -> Node \cup {None}]
  /\ active \in [Node -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ votesSeen \in [Node -> SUBSET Node]

Init ==
  /\ requested = {}
  /\ voteMsgs = {}
  /\ granted = [n \in Node |-> None]
  /\ active = [n \in Node |-> FALSE]
  /\ votesSeen = [n \in Node |-> {}]

\* A node broadcasts a request to become the exclusive holder of the resource.
Request(n) ==
  /\ ~active[n]
  /\ n \notin requested
  /\ requested' = requested \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<voteMsgs, granted, active, votesSeen>>

\* A voter grants its single outstanding vote to a requesting candidate; a
\* voter can hold only one live grant at a time, which forces any two
\* quorums for different candidates to intersect.
CastVote(v, c) ==
  /\ c \in requested
  /\ granted[v] = None
  /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![v] = c]
  /\ voteMsgs' = voteMsgs \cup {<<v, c>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, active, votesSeen>>

\* Vote messages sit in an unordered set and may be counted in any order or
\* after arbitrary delay, modeling network reordering; only a vote that is
\* still currently granted (fresh, not stale/superseded) may be counted.
CountVote(c, v) ==
  /\ <<v, c>> \in voteMsgs
  /\ granted[v] = c
  /\ v \notin votesSeen[c]
  /\ votesSeen' = [votesSeen EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {v}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, voteMsgs, granted, active>>

\* Once a candidate has collected votes from a quorum of nodes it claims
\* exclusive access to the critical resource.
BecomeActive(c) ==
  /\ ~active[c]
  /\ Cardinality(votesSeen[c]) >= Quorum
  /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<requested, voteMsgs, granted, votesSeen>>

\* Releasing the resource frees every voter that had granted this holder and
\* wipes its ballot record, so later rounds cannot reuse stale grants/votes.
Release(n) ==
  /\ active[n]
  /\ active' = [active EXCEPT ![n] = FALSE]
  /\ requested' = requested \ {n}
  /\ granted' = [x \in Node |-> IF granted[x] = n THEN None ELSE granted[x]]
  /\ votesSeen' = [votesSeen EXCEPT ![n] = {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED voteMsgs

Next ==
  \/ \E n \in Node : Request(n)
  \/ \E v, c \in Node : CastVote(v, c)
  \/ \E c, v \in Node : CountVote(c, v)
  \/ \E c \in Node : BecomeActive(c)
  \/ \E n \in Node : Release(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: no two distinct nodes may simultaneously hold the exclusive lock
\* on the critical resource, even though vote messages can be reordered.
MutualExclusion == \A n1, n2 \in Node : (active[n1] /\ active[n2]) => n1 = n2

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Node = {n1, n2, n3}

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT MutualExclusion

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A small cluster of game-lobby matchmaker nodes coordinates who is allowed to
hold exclusive control of a single critical resource (for example, the slot
that finalizes and starts a match for a lobby). Any node may broadcast a
request to become the resource's holder. Other nodes act as voters: each
voter can have only one outstanding vote granted at a time, and grants it to
whichever candidate it currently supports. Votes travel as messages that can
be reordered, delayed, or counted well after they were cast, and a candidate
becomes the active holder once it has collected votes from a quorum
(strict majority) of nodes. Only a vote that is still currently granted to
that candidate (not stale or superseded by the voter granting elsewhere) may
be counted, and releasing the resource clears the outstanding grants and
vote tallies tied to that holder so a later round cannot resurrect old
votes. Because any two quorums of a majority must share at least one common
voter, and that voter can only ever have one live grant outstanding, two
different candidates cannot both simultaneously accumulate a full quorum's
worth of currently-valid votes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct matchmaker nodes ever simultaneously hold exclusive access to the critical resource, even though vote messages may arrive out of order.

---- MODULE W4Od6m6p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Two independent elevator-control instances (1 and 2) share ONE physical
\* cabin-capacity pool. Each instance runs its own lease-based admission
\* cycle: idle -> boarding -> transit -> idle. A lease is only an admission
\* token for boarding; the safety property below is about the shared
\* physical occupancy pool, not about mutual exclusion of the lease itself.

CONSTANTS Cap, MaxWait

VARIABLES occ1, occ2, mode1, mode2, wait1, wait2

vars == <<occ1, occ2, mode1, mode2, wait1, wait2>>

Init ==
  /\ occ1 = 0
  /\ occ2 = 0
  /\ mode1 = "idle"
  /\ mode2 = "idle"
  /\ wait1 = 0
  /\ wait2 = 0

Arrive1 ==
  /\ wait1 < MaxWait
  /\ wait1' = wait1 + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode1, mode2, wait2>>

Arrive2 ==
  /\ wait2 < MaxWait
  /\ wait2' = wait2 + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode1, mode2, wait1>>

\* Acquiring the lease only starts a boarding window; it grants no
\* occupancy by itself.
StartBoarding1 ==
  /\ mode1 = "idle"
  /\ wait1 > 0
  /\ mode1' = "boarding"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode2, wait1, wait2>>

StartBoarding2 ==
  /\ mode2 = "idle"
  /\ wait2 > 0
  /\ mode2' = "boarding"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode1, wait1, wait2>>

\* Boarding is admitted only while the combined occupancy of BOTH
\* instances stays under the shared physical capacity Cap.
Board1 ==
  /\ mode1 = "boarding"
  /\ wait1 > 0
  /\ occ1 + occ2 < Cap
  /\ occ1' = occ1 + 1
  /\ wait1' = wait1 - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ2, mode1, mode2, wait2>>

Board2 ==
  /\ mode2 = "boarding"
  /\ wait2 > 0
  /\ occ1 + occ2 < Cap
  /\ occ2' = occ2 + 1
  /\ wait2' = wait2 - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, mode1, mode2, wait1>>

\* The lease expires (or the controller closes the doors) ending the
\* boarding window, whether or not it is full.
Depart1 ==
  /\ mode1 = "boarding"
  /\ mode1' = "transit"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode2, wait1, wait2>>

Depart2 ==
  /\ mode2 = "boarding"
  /\ mode2' = "transit"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, occ2, mode1, wait1, wait2>>

\* Unloading releases the lease and frees every seat this instance held
\* in the shared pool, atomically returning it to idle.
Unload1 ==
  /\ mode1 = "transit"
  /\ occ1' = 0
  /\ mode1' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ2, mode2, wait1, wait2>>

Unload2 ==
  /\ mode2 = "transit"
  /\ occ2' = 0
  /\ mode2' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<occ1, mode1, wait1, wait2>>

Next ==
  \/ Arrive1 \/ Arrive2
  \/ StartBoarding1 \/ StartBoarding2
  \/ Board1 \/ Board2
  \/ Depart1 \/ Depart2
  \/ Unload1 \/ Unload2

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(Depart1) /\ WF_vars(Unload1)
  /\ WF_vars(Depart2) /\ WF_vars(Unload2)

\* SAFETY: the shared physical cabin pool can never hold more passengers
\* than its capacity, no matter how the two independent instances interleave.
CapacityOK == occ1 + occ2 <= Cap

\* LIVENESS: whichever instance boards passengers, that instance's
\* occupancy eventually returns to zero (the trip completes and unloads).
EventuallyEmpties ==
  /\ (occ1 > 0 ~> occ1 = 0)
  /\ (occ2 > 0 ~> occ2 = 0)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Cap = 3
  MaxWait = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacityOK

PROPERTY EventuallyEmpties

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a skyscraper's elevator bank, two independent elevator-control instances each run their own lease-based boarding cycle, but both instances load passengers into a single shared physical cabin whose capacity is fixed. Each instance cycles through idle, boarding, and transit states: it acquires a lease to open a boarding window, admits waiting passengers one at a time into the shared cabin pool as long as the combined occupancy of both instances stays under the pool's capacity, then the lease expires (or the controller closes the doors), moving the instance to transit, and finally the cabin unloads, atomically freeing every seat that instance held and returning it to idle so a new lease cycle can begin. Because the lease only gates admission and not physical space, the two instances can race to fill the one shared pool, and only the combined occupancy check keeps the cabin from being overloaded.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The combined occupancy of both elevator-control instances never exceeds the shared cabin's capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever an instance has boarded at least one passenger into the shared cabin, that instance's occupancy eventually returns to zero once its trip completes and it unloads.

---- MODULE W4Od14m0p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Slots, NoSlot, MaxVer

VARIABLES droneSlot, slotVersion, pendingSlot, pendingVer, droneStatus

vars == <<droneSlot, slotVersion, pendingSlot, pendingVer, droneStatus>>

\* Optimistic locking: a drone reads a slot's version stamp, then tries to
\* commit; the commit only succeeds if the version is unchanged, else retry.

SlotFree(s) == \A d \in Drones : droneSlot[d] # s

Init ==
  /\ droneSlot = [d \in Drones |-> NoSlot]
  /\ slotVersion = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ pendingSlot = [d \in Drones |-> NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVer = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ droneStatus = [d \in Drones |-> "active"]

\* Drone begins a claim attempt: snapshot the slot's current version.
ReadVersion(d) ==
  /\ droneStatus[d] = "active"
  /\ droneSlot[d] = NoSlot
  /\ pendingSlot[d] = NoSlot
  /\ \E s \in Slots :
       /\ SlotFree(s)
       /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![d] = s]
       /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![d] = slotVersion[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<droneSlot, slotVersion, droneStatus>>

\* Optimistic commit: only succeeds if the version stamp still matches;
\* this check is the sole guard against two drones claiming one slot.
CommitClaim(d) ==
  /\ droneStatus[d] = "active"
  /\ pendingSlot[d] # NoSlot
  /\ slotVersion[pendingSlot[d]] = pendingVer[d]
  /\ slotVersion[pendingSlot[d]] < MaxVer
  /\ droneSlot' = [droneSlot EXCEPT ![d] = pendingSlot[d]]
  /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![pendingSlot[d]] = @ + 1]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![d] = NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED droneStatus

\* Version stamp moved on: the optimistic write lost the race, so retry
\* by abandoning the stale attempt (the drone re-reads on a later step).
RetryClaim(d) ==
  /\ droneStatus[d] = "active"
  /\ pendingSlot[d] # NoSlot
  /\ slotVersion[pendingSlot[d]] # pendingVer[d]
  /\ pendingSlot' = [pendingSlot EXCEPT ![d] = NoSlot]
  /\ pendingVer' = [pendingVer EXCEPT ![d] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<droneSlot, slotVersion, droneStatus>>

\* Drone finishes patrol and releases its slot, bumping the version stamp.
ReleaseSlot(d) ==
  /\ droneStatus[d] = "active"
  /\ droneSlot[d] # NoSlot
  /\ slotVersion[droneSlot[d]] < MaxVer
  /\ slotVersion' = [slotVersion EXCEPT ![droneSlot[d]] = @ + 1]
  /\ droneSlot' = [droneSlot EXCEPT ![d] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingSlot, pendingVer, droneStatus>>

\* The twist: a drone can crash silently at any time, freezing its state
\* forever (it never releases a held slot nor completes a pending claim).
CrashDrone(d) ==
  /\ droneStatus[d] = "active"
  /\ droneStatus' = [droneStatus EXCEPT ![d] = "crashed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<droneSlot, slotVersion, pendingSlot, pendingVer>>

Next ==
  \E d \in Drones :
    \/ ReadVersion(d)
    \/ CommitClaim(d)
    \/ RetryClaim(d)
    \/ ReleaseSlot(d)
    \/ CrashDrone(d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: no two distinct drones ever hold the same real slot at once.
\* This restates the literal "no double allocation" requirement as
\* per-slot-owner uniqueness across drones (a discouraged shape, used
\* here because it IS the required property for this cell).
SlotUniqueness ==
  \A d1, d2 \in Drones :
    (droneSlot[d1] = droneSlot[d2] /\ droneSlot[d1] # NoSlot) => d1 = d2

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
  Slots = {s1, s2}
  NoSlot = NoSlot
  MaxVer = 2

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT SlotUniqueness

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A small wildfire drone surveillance swarm patrols a wildfire perimeter using a fixed set of patrol slots (fixed vantage positions over the fire line). Drones claim exclusive ownership of a slot using optimistic locking with retry: a drone first reads the slot's current version stamp, then attempts to commit its claim, but the commit only succeeds if the version stamp is still unchanged since it was read; if another drone has already claimed (or released) that slot in the meantime, the version stamp has moved on, the optimistic write is rejected, and the drone must abandon the stale attempt and retry from scratch. A drone that finishes its patrol releases its slot, which also bumps the version stamp so that any concurrent claim attempt against that slot is invalidated. As a twist, one drone can crash silently at any time: it simply stops taking any further action, whether or not it is mid-claim or already holding a slot, without ever releasing what it held.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No two distinct drones ever simultaneously hold the same patrol slot (no double allocation of the same slot).

---- MODULE W4Od4m7p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, SlowCar, Capacity, NormalWashTime, SlowWashTime

ASSUME SlowCar \in Cars
ASSUME Capacity \in Nat \ {0}

VARIABLES notArrived, queue, inBay, casReg, progress, done

vars == <<notArrived, queue, inBay, casReg, progress, done>>

\* The slow car is not failed, just slower: it needs more Wash steps to
\* finish, but the number of steps is always finite so it never stalls forever.
WashTime(c) == IF c = SlowCar THEN SlowWashTime ELSE NormalWashTime

TypeOK == /\ notArrived \subseteq Cars
          /\ queue \in Seq(Cars)
          /\ inBay \subseteq Cars
          /\ casReg \in Nat
          /\ progress \in [Cars -> Nat]
          /\ done \subseteq Cars

Init == /\ notArrived = Cars
        /\ queue = <<>>
        /\ inBay = {}
        /\ casReg = 0
        /\ progress = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
        /\ done = {}

ArriveCar(c) == /\ c \in notArrived
                /\ notArrived' = notArrived \ {c}
                /\ queue' = Append(queue, c)
                /\ UNCHANGED <<inBay, casReg, progress, done>>

\* Admission is CAS-protected: read casReg, compare it against Capacity, and
\* only if there is spare room does the swap to casReg+1 happen, together
\* with seating the head-of-queue car in the bay.
AdmitHead == /\ queue # <<>>
             /\ casReg < Capacity
             /\ LET c == Head(queue)
                IN /\ inBay' = inBay \cup {c}
                   /\ casReg' = casReg + 1
                   /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
                   /\ progress' = [progress EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<notArrived, done>>

WashCar(c) == /\ c \in inBay
              /\ progress[c] < WashTime(c)
              /\ progress' = [progress EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<notArrived, queue, inBay, casReg, done>>

\* Departure frees the bay slot and decrements the CAS register in lockstep
\* with the actual occupancy, so the register never drifts from reality.
DepartCar(c) == /\ c \in inBay
                /\ progress[c] >= WashTime(c)
                /\ inBay' = inBay \ {c}
                /\ casReg' = casReg - 1
                /\ done' = done \cup {c}
                /\ UNCHANGED <<notArrived, queue, progress>>

Arrive == \E c \in Cars : ArriveCar(c)
Wash == \E c \in Cars : WashCar(c)
Depart == \E c \in Cars : DepartCar(c)

Next == Arrive \/ AdmitHead \/ Wash \/ Depart

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Arrive) /\ WF_vars(AdmitHead)
             /\ WF_vars(Wash) /\ WF_vars(Depart)

\* Safety: the CAS register may never claim more occupancy than the physical
\* bay has room for, and it must always match the true number of parked cars.
CapacityInvariant == /\ casReg <= Capacity
                     /\ casReg = Cardinality(inBay)

\* Liveness: every car that arrives, including the slow one, is eventually
\* admitted, finishes washing, and departs.
AllCarsEventuallyDone == <>(done = Cars)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    SlowCar = c1
    Capacity = 2
    NormalWashTime = 2
    SlowWashTime = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityInvariant
PROPERTY AllCarsEventuallyDone
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A small car-wash conveyor line has a bay with a fixed number of slots. Cars
arrive one at a time and queue up outside the bay. Admission into the bay is
guarded by a compare-and-swap register that tracks the current occupancy: a
waiting car may enter only if the register shows spare capacity, and entering
atomically swaps the register from its old count to old+1. Once inside, a car
washes by taking progress steps; most cars need only a couple of steps, but
one designated car is simply slow (not failed) and needs several more steps
before it is done. When a car finishes washing it departs, atomically
swapping the CAS register back down and freeing its slot for the next waiting
car.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The CAS register never exceeds the bay's physical capacity and always equals the true number of cars currently parked in the bay.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every car that arrives, including the slow car, is eventually admitted, finishes washing, and departs.

---- MODULE W4Od10m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Capacity, MaxId

\* A signalling block holds a bounded buffer (queue) of pending movement-
\* authority messages plus a set of messages already dispatched downstream
\* but not yet acknowledged (inflight). Both occupy the block's physical
\* capacity until acknowledged, since the block cannot be released early.
VARIABLES queue, inflight, acked, nextId, backpressure

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq(1..MaxId)
  /\ inflight \subseteq 1..MaxId
  /\ acked \subseteq 1..MaxId
  /\ nextId \in 1..(MaxId + 1)
  /\ backpressure \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ acked = {}
  /\ nextId = 1
  /\ backpressure = FALSE

\* Enqueue a fresh message only if the block still has spare capacity once
\* both buffered and inflight (unacked) messages are counted together.
Enqueue ==
  /\ nextId <= MaxId
  /\ Len(queue) + Cardinality(inflight) < Capacity
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextId)
  /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, acked>>
  /\ backpressure' = (Len(queue') + Cardinality(inflight') >= Capacity)

\* Twist: messages in the buffer may be reordered before they are
\* dispatched, modeling out-of-order delivery/processing on the block.
Reorder ==
  /\ Len(queue) > 1
  /\ \E i \in 1..(Len(queue) - 1):
       queue' = [queue EXCEPT ![i] = queue[i+1], ![i+1] = queue[i]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, acked, nextId, backpressure>>

\* Dispatch the head of the buffer downstream; it still occupies capacity
\* as an inflight message until acknowledged.
Dispatch ==
  /\ Len(queue) > 0
  /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
  /\ inflight' = inflight \union {Head(queue)}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, nextId>>
  /\ backpressure' = (Len(queue') + Cardinality(inflight') >= Capacity)

\* Acknowledgments may arrive out of order too (the twist applies
\* downstream as well): any inflight message can be acked next.
Ack ==
  /\ inflight # {}
  /\ \E m \in inflight:
       /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
       /\ acked' = acked \union {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, nextId>>
  /\ backpressure' = (Len(queue') + Cardinality(inflight') >= Capacity)

Next == Enqueue \/ Reorder \/ Dispatch \/ Ack

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, inflight, acked, nextId, backpressure>>

\* SAFETY: the signalling block's occupied capacity -- buffered plus
\* inflight unacknowledged messages -- never exceeds its physical bound,
\* regardless of how messages are reordered or acknowledged out of order.
CapacityInvariant == Len(queue) + Cardinality(inflight) <= Capacity

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Capacity = 3
    MaxId = 4

SPECIFICATION Spec

INVARIANT CapacityInvariant

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway signalling block manages a bounded work queue of movement-authority
messages awaiting processing, plus a set of messages already dispatched
downstream that are still unacknowledged. Because the block cannot be
released until an acknowledgment is received, both buffered and inflight
messages count against its fixed physical capacity, and the block signals
backpressure as it nears that limit. Messages may be reordered while queued,
and acknowledgments for dispatched messages may also arrive out of order,
reflecting real network and processing jitter between signalling blocks.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of buffered plus inflight unacknowledged messages
at a signalling block never exceeds its fixed capacity, even under arbitrary
reordering of queued messages and out-of-order acknowledgments.

---- MODULE W4Od7m4p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Cranes, QueueCap, NoHolder

VARIABLES queue, holder, status, crashed

vars == <<queue, holder, status, crashed>>

\* queue: FIFO of cranes waiting for the single exclusive berth/gantry slot (bounded => backpressure)
\* status: per-crane lifecycle; holder: the crane (if any) currently granted exclusive access
\* crashed: cranes whose operator silently died mid-hold, needing a controller timeout to reclaim the mutex

TypeOK == /\ queue \in Seq(Cranes)
          /\ Len(queue) <= QueueCap
          /\ holder \in Cranes \cup {NoHolder}
          /\ status \in [Cranes -> {"idle", "queued", "holding", "crashed"}]
          /\ crashed \subseteq Cranes

Init == /\ queue = <<>>
        /\ holder = NoHolder
        /\ status = [c \in Cranes |-> "idle"]
        /\ crashed = {}

\* Enqueue: an idle crane requests exclusive access; bounded queue enforces admission backpressure
Enqueue == \E c \in Cranes:
             /\ status[c] = "idle"
             /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap

             /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "queued"]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

\* Admit: the FIFO head of the queue is granted the mutex once it is free
Admit == /\ queue # <<>>
         /\ holder = NoHolder
         /\ holder' = Head(queue)
         /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "holding"]
         /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
         /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* Release: the current holder finishes its lift and honestly frees the mutex
Release == \E c \in Cranes:
             /\ holder = c
             /\ status[c] = "holding"
             /\ holder' = NoHolder
             /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed>>

\* Crash: the holding crane's operator silently crashes mid-hold and never itself releases

           /\ status[c] = "holding"
           /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
           /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![c] = "crashed"]
           /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holder>>

\* TimeoutRelease: the yard controller detects the silent crash and reclaims the mutex for others
TimeoutRelease == \E c \in Cranes:
                    /\ holder = c
                    /\ c \in crashed
                    /\ holder' = NoHolder
                    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, status, crashed>>

Next == Enqueue \/ Admit \/ Release \/ Crash \/ TimeoutRelease

             /\ WF_vars(Enqueue) /\ WF_vars(Admit)
             /\ WF_vars(Release) /\ WF_vars(TimeoutRelease)

\* MUTEX: no two distinct cranes ever both hold the exclusive berth/gantry slot at once
MutexOK == \A c1, c2 \in Cranes: (status[c1] = "holding" /\ status[c2] = "holding") => c1 = c2

Granted == \A c \in Cranes: (status[c] = "queued") ~> (status[c] = "holding")

\* An engine may acquire it only via compare-and-swap from NONE to itself,
\* and release it only by comparing its own id before swapping back to NONE.

  /\ engineState \in [Engines -> {"idle", "trying", "holding", "done"}]
  /\ price \in Prices \cup {NoPrice}
  /\ slowOrder \in {"idle", "inflight", "matched"}
  /\ phase \in {"open", "closed"}

  /\ cas = NONE
  /\ engineState = [e \in Engines |-> "idle"]
  /\ price = NoPrice
  /\ slowOrder = "idle"
  /\ phase = "open"

\* Compare-and-swap acquire: succeeds only when the register currently reads NONE.
CASAcquire(e) ==
  /\ phase = "open"
  /\ cas = NONE
  /\ engineState[e] = "idle"
  /\ cas' = e
  /\ engineState' = [engineState EXCEPT ![e] = "holding"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<price, slowOrder, phase>>

\* Only the current CAS holder may set the opening auction price.
CASSetPrice(e) ==
  /\ engineState[e] = "holding"
  /\ cas = e
  /\ price = NoPrice
  /\ \E p \in Prices : price' = p
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cas, engineState, slowOrder, phase>>

\* Release is itself a compare-and-swap: swap cas from e back to NONE.
CASRelease(e) ==
  /\ engineState[e] = "holding"
  /\ cas = e
  /\ price # NoPrice
  /\ cas' = NONE
  /\ engineState' = [engineState EXCEPT ![e] = "done"]
  /\ phase' = "closed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<price, slowOrder>>

\* merely delayed, so it never touches the CAS register itself.
SlowOrderArrive ==

  /\ slowOrder' = "inflight"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cas, engineState, price, phase>>

\* The slow order only matches once an opening price exists, regardless of
\* which engine holds or held the CAS lock.
SlowOrderMatch ==
  /\ slowOrder = "inflight"
  /\ price # NoPrice
  /\ slowOrder' = "matched"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cas, engineState, price, phase>>

  \/ (\E e \in Engines : CASAcquire(e))
  \/ (\E e \in Engines : CASSetPrice(e))
  \/ (\E e \in Engines : CASRelease(e))

  /\ Cardinality(fineHolders) <= 1

\* granted -- the shared pool never starves a requester forever.

  /\ (stateA = "wantF" ~> stateA = "hasF")

settlement-instance workers (A and B) that both operate over one shared
ledger. To touch the ledger, a worker must first acquire a coarse,
bank-level lock, then a fine, account-level lock, before performing its
settlement work and releasing both locks -- a classic coarse-then-fine

are independent processes but draw from the SAME lock pool, so a bug that
let either instance's fine-grained lock be granted while the other
instance already holds it (or holds the coarse lock) would let both
instances mutate the ledger's critical account state at once.

necessarily also the coarse-lock holder, so the two instances can never
simultaneously touch the critical ledger resource.

settlement instance is eventually granted -- the shared lock pool never
starves a requester forever.

VARIABLES term, leader, status, allocatedSlots, allocLog

NoLeader == "none"

Records == [slot: Slots, owner: Participants, term: 0..MaxTerm]

  /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
  /\ leader \in Participants \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ status \in {"up", "crashed"}
  /\ allocatedSlots \subseteq Slots

Init ==

  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ status = "up"
  /\ allocatedSlots = {}
  /\ allocLog = {}

\* First election: with nobody in charge yet, any participant may become leader of a fresh term
Elect ==

  /\ term < MaxTerm
  /\ \E p \in Participants :

       /\ term' = term + 1
       /\ status' = "up"

\* double-booked to two different (owner, term) pairs, i.e. no leader/failover split-brain
\* double allocation of the same dispensing slot.

EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS MsgIds, TotalPlayers, MaxVersion, MaxAborted

VARIABLES counts, version, pending, aborted, lastCommitted

vars == <<counts, version, pending, aborted, lastCommitted>>

\* The three pools a player can occupy in the matchmaker pipeline
Pools == {"Queue", "Match", "Lobby"}

MsgType == [active: BOOLEAN, src: Pools, dst: Pools, amt: 1..TotalPlayers, ver: 0..(MaxVersion - 1)]

RECURSIVE SumSet(_, _)
\* Recursive helper to sum a function's values over a finite domain subset
SumSet(S, f) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
       IN f[x] + SumSet(S \ {x}, f)

PendingAmt(id) == IF pending[id].active THEN pending[id].amt ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
  /\ counts \in [Pools -> 0..TotalPlayers]
  /\ version \in 0..(MaxVersion - 1)
  /\ pending \in [MsgIds -> MsgType]
  /\ aborted \in 0..MaxAborted
  /\ lastCommitted \in MsgType

\* Every player is either resting in a pool or reserved inside an in-flight CAS request
Conservation ==
  SumSet(Pools, counts) + SumSet(MsgIds, [id \in MsgIds |-> PendingAmt(id)]) = TotalPlayers

Init ==
  /\ counts = [p \in Pools |-> IF p = "Queue" THEN TotalPlayers ELSE 0]
  /\ version = 0
  /\ pending = [id \in MsgIds |-> [active |-> FALSE, src |-> "Queue", dst |-> "Queue", amt |-> 1, ver |-> 0]]
  /\ aborted = 0
  /\ lastCommitted = [active |-> FALSE, src |-> "Queue", dst |-> "Queue", amt |-> 1, ver |-> 0]

\* Request reserves amt players out of src right away, snapshotting the CAS register's version
Request(id, src, dst, amt) ==
  /\ ~pending[id].active
  /\ src # dst
  /\ amt <= counts[src]
  /\ counts' = [counts EXCEPT ![src] = counts[src] - amt]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![id] = [active |-> TRUE, src |-> src, dst |-> dst, amt |-> amt, ver |-> version]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, aborted, lastCommitted>>

\* Commit succeeds only if the CAS register's version still matches what was snapshotted
Commit(id) ==
  /\ pending[id].active
  /\ pending[id].ver = version
  /\ counts' = [counts EXCEPT ![pending[id].dst] = counts[pending[id].dst] + pending[id].amt]
  /\ lastCommitted' = [pending[id] EXCEPT !.active = TRUE]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![id] = [active |-> FALSE, src |-> "Queue", dst |-> "Queue", amt |-> 1, ver |-> 0]]
  /\ version' = (version + 1) % MaxVersion
  /\ UNCHANGED aborted

\* A stale request, whose snapshot was overtaken by a reordered commit, re-reads the version
Retry(id) ==
  /\ pending[id].active
  /\ pending[id].ver # version
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![id].ver = version]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<counts, version, aborted, lastCommitted>>

\* Abort gives up on a stale reservation and returns the reserved players to their source pool
Abort(id) ==
  /\ pending[id].active
  /\ pending[id].ver # version
  /\ aborted < MaxAborted
  /\ counts' = [counts EXCEPT ![pending[id].src] = counts[pending[id].src] + pending[id].amt]
  /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![id] = [active |-> FALSE, src |-> "Queue", dst |-> "Queue", amt |-> 1, ver |-> 0]]
  /\ aborted' = aborted + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, lastCommitted>>

  \/ \E id \in MsgIds, src \in Pools, dst \in Pools, amt \in 1..TotalPlayers : Request(id, src, dst, amt)
  \/ \E id \in MsgIds : Commit(id)
  \/ \E id \in MsgIds : Retry(id)
  \/ \E id \in MsgIds : Abort(id)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CONSTANTS
  MsgIds = {1, 2}
  TotalPlayers = 2
  MaxVersion = 2
  MaxAborted = 1

INVARIANT Conservation

CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker moves players between three pools: Queue (waiting for a match), Match (grouped and being finalized), and Lobby (ready to play). Player-count bookkeeping between pools is protected by a single compare-and-swap (CAS) register: a version number. To move a batch of players from one pool to another, a worker first reserves that batch out of the source pool and snapshots the current CAS version, then later tries to commit the move by comparing its snapshotted version against the live version. If the versions still match, the commit applies atomically and bumps the version; if some other commit slipped in first (because worker messages can be delayed, duplicated in effect, or reordered across the network), the version has moved on, so the commit is rejected and the worker either retries with a fresh version snapshot or aborts and refunds the reserved players back to the source pool. Because commits and retries/aborts can be interleaved in any order, a reserved batch may sit "in flight" for a while before it is finally applied or refunded, but every player must be accounted for at all times: resting in a pool, or held in exactly one in-flight reservation.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of players resting across the Queue/Match/Lobby pools plus the players held in in-flight (not yet committed or aborted) CAS reservations always equals the fixed total player count, regardless of how CAS commit/retry/abort messages get reordered.

\* inventory count) with an append-only commit log. Nodes propose a new

\* acks has formed AND the proposal is still fresh (proposal.base = version).
\* An admin may bypass the quorum entirely, but always writes against the
\* live version and clears any in-flight round so a stale quorum can never
\* silently clobber the admin's write (the "no lost update" guarantee).

  /\ record = CHOOSE v \in Values : TRUE
  /\ version = 0
  /\ proposal = [val |-> record, base |-> 0]
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ mode = "Idle"
  /\ history = <<record>>

Propose(n, v) ==
  /\ mode = "Idle"
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ proposal' = [val |-> v, base |-> version]
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ mode' = "Voting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, history>>

ProposeAny == \E n \in Nodes, v \in Values : Propose(n, v)

Ack(n) ==
  /\ mode = "Voting"
  /\ n \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, proposal, mode, history>>

AckAny == \E n \in Nodes : Ack(n)

\* QuorumCommit only applies the proposed value if it is still based on the
\* current version -- otherwise a competing (e.g. admin) write already moved
\* the record forward and this stale proposal must not overwrite it.
QuorumCommit ==
  /\ mode = "Voting"
  /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum
  /\ proposal.base = version
  /\ record' = proposal.val
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ history' = Append(history, proposal.val)
  /\ mode' = "Idle"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED proposal

\* AdminOverride bypasses quorum acknowledgment, but always writes against
\* the live version and discards any in-flight (now-stale) proposal round.
AdminOverride(v) ==
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ record' = v
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ history' = Append(history, v)
  /\ mode' = "Idle"
  /\ votes' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED proposal

AdminAny == \E v \in Values : AdminOverride(v)

Next == ProposeAny \/ AckAny \/ QuorumCommit \/ AdminAny

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(AckAny) /\ WF_vars(QuorumCommit) /\ WF_vars(AdminAny)

\* Safety: the log never has gaps or duplicates (Len tracks version exactly),
\* the visible record always equals the newest log entry, and whenever a
\* quorum has actually formed for the pending proposal it is still validated
\* against the live version -- so a quorum vote can never be used to commit
\* an update that silently discards a newer (e.g. admin) write.
NoLostUpdates ==
  /\ Len(history) = version + 1
  /\ record = history[version + 1]
  /\ (mode = "Voting" /\ Cardinality(votes) >= Quorum) => proposal.base = version

\* Liveness: once a proposal round starts, it always eventually resolves
\* (via quorum commit or admin override) -- votes never accumulate forever
\* on a proposal that is left hanging.
VotingResolves == mode = "Voting" ~> mode = "Idle"

SPECIFICATION Spec

A small network of vending machines shares one authoritative record (a price or inventory count) that any machine may propose to update. To change the record, a machine broadcasts a proposal tagged with the version of the record it read; other machines acknowledge (vote for) that proposal, and once a quorum of acknowledgments has formed AND the proposal is still based on the current version, the update is committed and appended to an audit log. A privileged admin machine may bypass the quorum-voting process entirely and override the record directly, but it always writes against the live version and clears out any in-flight proposal round, so a quorum that formed on stale information can never sneak through afterward and silently discard the admin's write. Committed values and their versions are tracked in an append-only log so the currently visible record is always traceable to the most recent commit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a quorum has genuinely formed for the pending proposal, that proposal is still validated against the live version (and the visible record always equals the newest append-only log entry), so no committed update to the shared price/inventory record is ever silently lost or overwritten by a stale quorum-approved write.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every proposal round that starts (quorum voting in progress) eventually resolves -- via quorum commit or admin override -- so votes never accumulate forever without the round being settled.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p0t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Participants, Quorum, NoCand

ASSUME NoCand \notin Participants
ASSUME Quorum \in Nat /\ Quorum <= Cardinality(Participants)

VARIABLES votes, holder, moving, slow

vars == <<votes, holder, moving, slow>>

\* votes[p] = participants who have cast a certifying vote for p to take command
\* holder   = participant currently certified (by quorum) to command the car, or NoCand
\* Quorum voting: p may become holder only after >= Quorum distinct votes for p

TypeOK ==
  /\ votes \in [Participants -> SUBSET Participants]
  /\ holder \in Participants \cup {NoCand}
  /\ moving \in BOOLEAN
  /\ slow \subseteq Participants

Init ==
  /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> {}]
  /\ holder = NoCand
  /\ moving = FALSE
  /\ slow = {}

\* Campaigns for command may only run while the car is uncommanded
Nominate(p) ==
  /\ holder = NoCand
  /\ votes[p] = {}
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = {p}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, moving, slow>>

CastVote(p, q) ==
  /\ holder = NoCand
  /\ votes[p] # {}
  /\ q \notin votes[p]
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {q}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, moving, slow>>

\* A participant becomes slow while boarding/responding; it keeps acting, just later -- never fails outright
MarkSlow(p) ==
  /\ p \notin slow
  /\ slow' = slow \cup {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holder, moving>>

ClearSlow(p) ==
  /\ p \in slow
  /\ slow' = slow \ {p}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holder, moving>>

\* Winning a quorum certifies exclusive command; every pending campaign bank-wide
\* is invalidated so no stale vote count can be reused after a holder takes command
AcquireControl(p) ==
  /\ holder = NoCand
  /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
  /\ holder' = p
  /\ votes' = [q \in Participants |-> {}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<moving, slow>>

StartMotion ==
  /\ holder # NoCand
  /\ ~moving
  /\ moving' = TRUE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holder, slow>>

StopMotion ==
  /\ moving
  /\ moving' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, holder, slow>>

Release ==
  /\ holder # NoCand
  /\ ~moving
  /\ holder' = NoCand
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, moving, slow>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Participants : Nominate(p)
  \/ \E p, q \in Participants : CastVote(p, q)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : MarkSlow(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : ClearSlow(p)
  \/ \E p \in Participants : AcquireControl(p)
  \/ StartMotion
  \/ StopMotion
  \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: while a holder has certified quorum command of the car (needed for
\* it to move), no other participant may simultaneously hold a competing
\* certified quorum of votes for itself -- true mutual exclusion of command.
MutualExclusion ==
  /\ (moving => holder # NoCand)
  /\ (holder # NoCand => \A q \in Participants \ {holder} : Cardinality(votes[q]) < Quorum)

---- MODULE W4Od15m7p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS A, B, S, OrderA, OrderB, OrderS

\* Fixed roster for the opening auction: A and B are ordinary submitters, S is the slow one
Participants == {A, B, S}
NotRead == -1

VARIABLES record, version, incorporated, snapshot

vars == <<record, version, incorporated, snapshot>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ record \in Int
    /\ version \in Int
    /\ incorporated \subseteq Participants
    /\ snapshot \in [Participants -> Int]

OrderOf(p) == IF p = A THEN OrderA ELSE IF p = B THEN OrderB ELSE OrderS

Init ==
    /\ record = 0
    /\ version = 0
    /\ incorporated = {}
    /\ snapshot = [p \in Participants |-> NotRead]

\* Before submitting, a participant snapshots the CAS version of the shared order-book record
TakeSnapshot(p) ==
    /\ p \notin incorporated
    /\ snapshot[p] = NotRead
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, incorporated>>

\* CAS succeeds only if version is unchanged since the snapshot: this is what prevents lost updates
CasSucceed(p) ==
    /\ p \notin incorporated
    /\ snapshot[p] # NotRead
    /\ snapshot[p] = version
    /\ record' = record + OrderOf(p)
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ incorporated' = incorporated \cup {p}
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = NotRead]

\* CAS fails if another order was incorporated first; p must retry with a fresh snapshot
CasFail(p) ==
    /\ p \notin incorporated
    /\ snapshot[p] # NotRead
    /\ snapshot[p] # version
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![p] = NotRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, incorporated>>

\* S may be slow to act (auction stays open for it), but it is never dropped or failed
SlowDefer ==
    /\ S \notin incorporated
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, version, incorporated, snapshot>>

Next ==
    \/ TakeSnapshot(A) \/ TakeSnapshot(B) \/ TakeSnapshot(S)
    \/ CasSucceed(A) \/ CasSucceed(B) \/ CasSucceed(S)
    \/ CasFail(A) \/ CasFail(B) \/ CasFail(S)
    \/ SlowDefer

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(TakeSnapshot(A)) /\ WF_vars(CasSucceed(A)) /\ WF_vars(CasFail(A))
    /\ WF_vars(TakeSnapshot(B)) /\ WF_vars(CasSucceed(B)) /\ WF_vars(CasFail(B))
    /\ WF_vars(TakeSnapshot(S)) /\ WF_vars(CasSucceed(S)) /\ WF_vars(CasFail(S))

SumOrders(set) ==
    (IF A \in set THEN OrderA ELSE 0)
    + (IF B \in set THEN OrderB ELSE 0)
    + (IF S \in set THEN OrderS ELSE 0)

\* Safety: the record always equals the sum of orders actually incorporated -- no update is ever lost or double-counted
NoLostUpdates == record = SumOrders(incorporated)

\* Liveness: every submitted order, including the slow submitter's, is eventually incorporated
EventuallyAllIncorporated == <>(incorporated = Participants)

The slow submitter is permitted to delay its snapshot/CAS attempt indefinitely relative to the others -- it is never dropped, timed out, or treated as failed -- but it is guaranteed to keep trying.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The order-book record always equals the sum of exactly the orders that have actually been incorporated via a successful CAS, so no submitted order is ever lost or double-counted despite concurrent retries.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Procs, Slots

VARIABLES sectionLock, slotLock, manifest, pending, phase, workSlot

vars == <<sectionLock, slotLock, manifest, pending, phase, workSlot>>

NoneVal == "none"

\* Coarse (yard-section) and fine (crane-slot) locks must be acquired in
\* that order before a process may compute and ship a manifest update.
Init ==
  /\ sectionLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoneVal]
  /\ slotLock    = [s \in Slots |-> NoneVal]
  /\ manifest    = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ pending     = {}
  /\ phase       = [p \in Procs |-> "idle"]
  /\ workSlot    = [p \in Procs |-> NoneVal]

AcquireSection(p, s) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "idle"
  /\ sectionLock[s] = NoneVal
  /\ sectionLock' = [sectionLock EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ workSlot'    = [workSlot EXCEPT ![p] = s]
  /\ phase'       = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "section"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, manifest, pending>>

AcquireSlot(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "section"
  /\ LET s == workSlot[p] IN
       /\ sectionLock[s] = p
       /\ slotLock[s] = NoneVal
       /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = p]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "slot"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sectionLock, manifest, pending, workSlot>>

\* Compute the new manifest value while holding both locks and hand it
\* off as an asynchronous message; the locks are NOT released yet.
SendUpdate(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "slot"
  /\ LET s == workSlot[p] IN
       /\ slotLock[s] = p
       /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<p, s, manifest[s] + 1>>}
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sectionLock, slotLock, manifest, workSlot>>

\* Messages sit in an unordered set, so delivery order across processes
\* and slots is arbitrary -- this is where reordering happens. Locks are
\* only released once the matching message is actually applied.
DeliverUpdate(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "waiting"
  /\ LET s   == workSlot[p]
         msg == CHOOSE m \in pending : m[1] = p /\ m[2] = s
     IN
       /\ manifest' = [manifest EXCEPT ![s] = msg[3]]
       /\ pending'  = pending \ {msg}
       /\ slotLock'    = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneVal]
       /\ sectionLock' = [sectionLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneVal]
       /\ workSlot' = [workSlot EXCEPT ![p] = NoneVal]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Procs, s \in Slots : AcquireSection(p, s)
  \/ \E p \in Procs : AcquireSlot(p)
  \/ \E p \in Procs : SendUpdate(p)
  \/ \E p \in Procs : DeliverUpdate(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: any in-flight (undelivered) update message must still equal
\* "current manifest value + 1" for its slot. If some other write had
\* slipped in underneath it, the message would be stale, and delivering
\* it would silently overwrite -- i.e. lose -- that intervening update.
NoLostUpdates ==
  \A m \in pending : m[3] = manifest[m[2]] + 1

\* Bounds the reachable state space: manifest values need not grow past
\* a handful of cycles to exercise every interesting interleaving.
StateBound ==
  \A s \in Slots : manifest[s] <= 3

====

CONSTANTS
  Procs = {p1, p2}
  Slots = {s1, s2}

SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CONSTRAINT StateBound
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
In a container-ship crane yard, a shared container-manifest record tracks
how many containers have been placed at each crane slot. Before a crane
operator's process may update the manifest for a slot, it must first
acquire the coarse yard-section lock covering that slot, and only then
the fine-grained crane-slot lock underneath it. Once both locks are held,
the process reads the manifest, computes the incremented value, and hands
it off as an asynchronous update message to the yard's manifest service
rather than writing it in place immediately. These update messages travel
over an unordered channel, so they can be delivered out of send order --
a message from one crane can be applied before or after a message from
another, and delivery for different slots can interleave arbitrarily. The
hierarchical locking discipline keeps this safe: a process does not
release its section and slot locks until its own update message has
actually been delivered and applied, so no other process can slip in a
conflicting read/write on the same slot while an update is still in
flight, even though reordering across slots and processes is otherwise
unconstrained.

SAFETY PROPERTY: every in-flight (undelivered) manifest-update message is
always still exactly one greater than the manifest's current value for
its slot, so no concurrently interleaved or reordered update can silently
overwrite -- lose -- another process's completed update.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m9p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Patrons, MaxEpoch, CapValues

VARIABLES status, requestEpoch, epoch, capacity

vars == <<status, requestEpoch, epoch, capacity>>

\* Epoch-guarded reconfiguration: capacity may only change via Reconfigure,
\* which bumps the epoch and must not revoke already-granted holds.
\* A reservation request is stamped with the epoch it was submitted in;
\* if the epoch has since advanced, the request is stale and gets rejected.

HeldCount == Cardinality({p \in Patrons : status[p] = "held"})

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in [Patrons -> {"idle", "waiting", "held"}]
    /\ requestEpoch \in [Patrons -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ capacity \in CapValues

\* SAFETY: number of active holds never exceeds the current capacity.
CapacityOK == HeldCount <= capacity

Init ==
    /\ status = [p \in Patrons |-> "idle"]
    /\ requestEpoch = [p \in Patrons |-> 0]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ capacity \in CapValues

Request(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "idle"
    /\ \A q \in Patrons : status[q] # "waiting"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "waiting"]
    /\ requestEpoch' = [requestEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

Grant(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "waiting"
    /\ requestEpoch[p] = epoch
    /\ HeldCount < capacity
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "held"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestEpoch, epoch, capacity>>

Reject(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "waiting"
    /\ requestEpoch[p] # epoch
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestEpoch, epoch, capacity>>

Release(p) ==
    /\ status[p] = "held"
    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requestEpoch, epoch, capacity>>

\* Reconfigure the hold-shelf capacity for a new epoch; it may never drop
\* capacity below the holds already outstanding.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ c \in CapValues
    /\ c >= HeldCount
    /\ capacity' = c
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, requestEpoch>>

RequestAny == \E p \in Patrons : Request(p)
GrantAny == \E p \in Patrons : Grant(p)
RejectAny == \E p \in Patrons : Reject(p)
ReleaseAny == \E p \in Patrons : Release(p)
ReconfigureAny == \E c \in CapValues : Reconfigure(c)

Next == RequestAny \/ GrantAny \/ RejectAny \/ ReleaseAny \/ ReconfigureAny

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ WF_vars(RequestAny)
        /\ WF_vars(GrantAny)
        /\ WF_vars(RejectAny)
        /\ WF_vars(ReleaseAny)
        /\ WF_vars(ReconfigureAny)

\* LIVENESS: any patron currently waiting is eventually resolved (granted
\* a hold or rejected), driven by Grant/Reject/Release/Reconfigure fairness.
Resolution == \A p \in Patrons : (status[p] = "waiting") ~> (status[p] # "waiting")

    MaxEpoch = 2
    CapValues = {1, 2}

PROPERTY Resolution

nl:
A small library manages a shared hold-shelf for reserved books using epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Each patron can submit a reservation request, which is granted a hold slot only if fewer holds are currently outstanding than the shelf's current capacity, or is rejected if the request has gone stale (i.e. the epoch has advanced since the request was submitted). The library staff can reconfigure the shelf's capacity at runtime, which bumps the epoch and immediately invalidates any pending request stamped with an older epoch -- but a reconfiguration is only allowed if the new capacity is not smaller than the number of holds already outstanding, since already-granted holds cannot be revoked. Patrons holding a book may release it at any time, freeing a slot for others.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of active reservation holds never exceeds the library's current runtime-configured capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every patron whose reservation request is pending is eventually either granted a hold slot or rejected due to a stale epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS CTRL, MaxEpoch

\* NoneC marks "no controller holds this lock".
NoneC == "none"

VARIABLES authEpoch, sectorHolder, slotHolder, slotEpoch, msgs

vars == <<authEpoch, sectorHolder, slotHolder, slotEpoch, msgs>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ authEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ sectorHolder \in CTRL \cup {NoneC}
  /\ slotHolder \in CTRL \cup {NoneC}
  /\ slotEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
  /\ msgs \subseteq [ctrl: CTRL, kind: {"sector", "slot"}, epoch: 0..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ authEpoch = 0
  /\ sectorHolder = NoneC
  /\ slotHolder = NoneC
  /\ slotEpoch = 0
  /\ msgs = {}

\* A controller may request the coarse sector lock only while it is free.
SendSectorReq(c) ==
  /\ sectorHolder = NoneC
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "sector", epoch |-> authEpoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, sectorHolder, slotHolder, slotEpoch>>

\* Grants re-check freshness at delivery time: the network may reorder
\* messages, so a stale-epoch sector request is simply never actionable.
GrantSector(c) ==
  /\ sectorHolder = NoneC
  /\ [ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "sector", epoch |-> authEpoch] \in msgs
  /\ sectorHolder' = c
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {[ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "sector", epoch |-> authEpoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, slotHolder, slotEpoch>>

\* Fine-grained requests are only sent by whoever currently owns the sector.
SendSlotReq(c) ==
  /\ sectorHolder = c
  /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {[ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "slot", epoch |-> authEpoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, sectorHolder, slotHolder, slotEpoch>>

\* The delivery-time recheck of sectorHolder = c is what defeats a reordered
\* slot-grant message from a controller who has since lost the sector lock.
GrantSlot(c) ==
  /\ sectorHolder = c
  /\ [ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "slot", epoch |-> authEpoch] \in msgs
  /\ slotHolder' = c
  /\ slotEpoch' = authEpoch
  /\ msgs' = msgs \ {[ctrl |-> c, kind |-> "slot", epoch |-> authEpoch]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, sectorHolder>>

ReleaseSlot(c) ==
  /\ slotHolder = c
  /\ slotHolder' = NoneC
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, sectorHolder, slotEpoch, msgs>>

\* Releasing the coarse lock also drops any fine slot grant under it.
ReleaseSector(c) ==
  /\ sectorHolder = c
  /\ sectorHolder' = NoneC
  /\ slotHolder' = NoneC
  /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, slotEpoch, msgs>>

\* A sector handoff bumps the epoch and revokes every outstanding lock and
\* message, so any older-epoch message becomes permanently stale.
Reauthorize ==
  /\ authEpoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ authEpoch' = authEpoch + 1
  /\ sectorHolder' = NoneC
  /\ slotHolder' = NoneC
  /\ slotEpoch' = 0
  /\ msgs' = {}

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in CTRL : SendSectorReq(c) \/ GrantSector(c)
                     \/ SendSlotReq(c) \/ GrantSlot(c)
                     \/ ReleaseSlot(c) \/ ReleaseSector(c)
  \/ Reauthorize

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the fine runway-slot lock may only be held by a controller who
\* is still the live, current-epoch sector holder -- never a stale or
\* unauthorized participant surviving a reordered message.
HierAuth ==
  \A c \in CTRL :
    slotHolder = c => (sectorHolder = c /\ slotEpoch = authEpoch)

nl:
A runway allocator coordinates aircraft handoffs across an airspace sector
using two hierarchical locks: a coarse sector lock (which controller owns
the whole sector right now) and a fine runway-slot lock (which controller
may actually clear an aircraft onto a specific runway), where the slot lock
may only be granted to whoever currently holds the sector lock. Controllers
communicate over a network where request and grant messages can be
reordered or delayed arbitrarily, so a slot-grant message sent while a
controller legitimately held the sector lock might only be processed after
that controller released the sector lock, after a sector reauthorization
handoff, or after another controller has taken over. The allocator tags
every authority-changing message with the current authorization epoch and
re-checks, at the moment a message is actually processed (not at the moment
it was sent), both the epoch and the live sector-lock holder, so that a
stale or reordered message from a controller who is no longer the current,
authorized sector holder can never be honored into a fine-grained runway
grant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a controller holds the fine runway-slot lock, that
same controller must currently also hold the coarse sector lock and its
slot grant must have been stamped with the authorization epoch that is
still in effect (never an unauthorized or stale participant grant).

---- MODULE W4Od16m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT Capacity

VARIABLES committed1, committed2, ver, req1, req2

vars == <<committed1, committed2, ver, req1, req2>>

\* req1/req2 model each dispenser's in-flight request: "idle" means no active
\* request; "committing" carries the version snapshot read at commit time.
Stages == {"idle", "committing"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ committed1 \in 0..Capacity
    /\ committed2 \in 0..Capacity
    /\ ver \in 0..Capacity
    /\ req1.stage \in Stages /\ req1.snap \in 0..Capacity
    /\ req2.stage \in Stages /\ req2.snap \in 0..Capacity

Init ==
    /\ committed1 = 0
    /\ committed2 = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ req1 = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]
    /\ req2 = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]

\* A dispenser picks up a new prescription and snapshots the shared version.
Request1 ==
    /\ req1.stage = "idle"
    /\ req1' = [stage |-> "committing", snap |-> ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req2>>

\* Optimistic commit: only succeeds if no one else changed the pool version
\* since this request's snapshot, and the shared pool still has room.
Commit1 ==
    /\ req1.stage = "committing"
    /\ req1.snap = ver
    /\ committed1 + committed2 < Capacity
    /\ committed1' = committed1 + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ req1' = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed2, req2>>

\* Version mismatch: some other commit landed since our snapshot, so retry
\* by re-reading the current version instead of overwriting anyone's update.
Retry1 ==
    /\ req1.stage = "committing"
    /\ req1.snap # ver
    /\ req1' = [stage |-> "committing", snap |-> ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req2>>

\* Version matches but the shared pool is already full: reject the request.
Reject1 ==
    /\ req1.stage = "committing"
    /\ req1.snap = ver
    /\ committed1 + committed2 >= Capacity
    /\ req1' = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req2>>

Request2 ==
    /\ req2.stage = "idle"
    /\ req2' = [stage |-> "committing", snap |-> ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req1>>

Commit2 ==
    /\ req2.stage = "committing"
    /\ req2.snap = ver
    /\ committed1 + committed2 < Capacity
    /\ committed2' = committed2 + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ req2' = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, req1>>

Retry2 ==
    /\ req2.stage = "committing"
    /\ req2.snap # ver
    /\ req2' = [stage |-> "committing", snap |-> ver]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req1>>

Reject2 ==
    /\ req2.stage = "committing"
    /\ req2.snap = ver
    /\ committed1 + committed2 >= Capacity
    /\ req2' = [stage |-> "idle", snap |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<committed1, committed2, ver, req1>>

Next ==
    \/ Request1 \/ Commit1 \/ Retry1 \/ Reject1
    \/ Request2 \/ Commit2 \/ Retry2 \/ Reject2

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Request1) /\ WF_vars(Commit1) /\ WF_vars(Retry1) /\ WF_vars(Reject1)
    /\ WF_vars(Request2) /\ WF_vars(Commit2) /\ WF_vars(Retry2) /\ WF_vars(Reject2)

\* SAFETY: the two independent dispensers draw from one shared pool, so the
\* combined committed total -- not either instance alone -- must stay bounded.
CapacityOK == committed1 + committed2 <= Capacity

\* LIVENESS: an in-flight optimistic-lock request never retries forever; it
\* is always eventually driven back to idle by a commit or a rejection.
Progress ==
    /\ [](req1.stage = "committing" => <>(req1.stage = "idle"))
    /\ [](req2.stage = "committing" => <>(req2.stage = "idle"))

\* AdminOverride models the privileged admin path: it bypasses the token
\* entirely but must atomically evict any prior occupant of the slot before
\* handing it to a new device, so the same slot is never double-allocated.

  /\ tokenHolder = RingOrder[1]

  /\ adminActive = FALSE

  /\ tokenHolder' = RingOrder[ringIndex']
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, adminActive>>

  \E s \in Slots :
     /\ ~ \E d2 \in Devices : <<s, d2>> \in allocated
     /\ allocated' = allocated \cup {<<s, tokenHolder>>}
     /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, ringIndex, adminActive>>

ReleaseSlot ==
  \E s \in Slots, d \in Devices :
     /\ <<s, d>> \in allocated
     /\ allocated' = allocated \ {<<s, d>>}
     /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, ringIndex, adminActive>>

  /\ \E s \in Slots, d \in Devices :
        allocated' = (allocated \ {p \in allocated : p[1] = s}) \cup {<<s, d>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenHolder, ringIndex, adminActive>>

  /\ adminActive' = ~adminActive
  /\ UNCHANGED <<allocated, tokenHolder, ringIndex>>

Next ==
  \/ PassToken
  \/ RequestSlot
  \/ ReleaseSlot
  \/ AdminOverride
  \/ ToggleAdmin

\* grant came from the token path or from the admin override path.

free access-code slot for itself; a device may later release a slot it holds.

any slot directly to a chosen device, bypassing the token requirement
entirely, but this override path must still hand out each slot to at most one
device at a time, exactly like the normal token-gated path.

EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Capacity, Deposits, Withdrawals

Units == Deposits \cup Withdrawals

VARIABLES count, network, pending, applied

vars == <<count, network, pending, applied>>

\* Delta(u) is the signed inventory change a CAS message for unit u carries:
\* +1 for a blood-unit deposit, -1 for a withdrawal.
Delta(u) == IF u \in Deposits THEN 1 ELSE -1

TypeOK ==
  /\ count \in 0..Capacity
  /\ pending \subseteq Units
  /\ applied \subseteq Units
  /\ network \subseteq [id : Units, old : 0..Capacity, delta : {-1, 1}]

Init ==
  /\ count = 0
  /\ network = {}
  /\ pending = Units
  /\ applied = {}

\* A station reads the current committed count and enqueues a CAS message
\* carrying that snapshot as its expected "old" value. The network is a
\* SET, not a sequence, so messages may be delivered in any order.
IssueDeposit ==
  \E u \in Deposits :
    /\ u \in pending
    /\ ~ \E m \in network : m.id = u
    /\ network' = network \cup {[id |-> u, old |-> count, delta |-> Delta(u)]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, pending, applied>>

IssueWithdrawal ==
  \E u \in Withdrawals :
    /\ u \in pending
    /\ ~ \E m \in network : m.id = u
    /\ network' = network \cup {[id |-> u, old |-> count, delta |-> Delta(u)]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, pending, applied>>

\* CAS commit: the message's snapshot "old" field must still match the
\* live register, and the result must respect the storage unit's capacity.
DeliverSuccess ==
  \E m \in network :
    /\ m.old = count
    /\ (count + m.delta) \in 0..Capacity
    /\ count' = count + m.delta
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {m.id}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {m.id}
    /\ network' = network \ {m}

\* A reordered / stale message fails its compare (or would breach capacity)
\* and is discarded; the station will re-issue with a fresh snapshot later.
DeliverFail ==
  \E m \in network :
    /\ \/ m.old # count
       \/ (count + m.delta) \notin 0..Capacity
    /\ network' = network \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, pending, applied>>

Next == IssueDeposit \/ IssueWithdrawal \/ DeliverSuccess \/ DeliverFail

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(IssueDeposit)
  /\ WF_vars(IssueWithdrawal)
  /\ WF_vars(DeliverSuccess)
  /\ WF_vars(DeliverFail)

\* SAFETY: the CAS-guarded commit above never lets count leave 0..Capacity,
\* i.e. the blood bank never records more units than the storage can hold.
CapacityOK == count \in 0..Capacity

\* LIVENESS: despite reordering-induced CAS failures and retries, every
\* pending inventory update is eventually applied.
AllApplied == \A u \in Units : (u \in pending) ~> (u \in applied)

Field stations submit deposit and withdrawal requests: each station snapshots the current count, computes the new count it wants to commit, and sends a CAS message (expected-old, new) to the register over a network that may reorder messages in transit. CONSTANTS Cars, NoCar, MaxTime, LeaseLen

ASSUME NoCar \notin Cars

VARIABLES holder, gen, expiry, clock, firedThisLease, totalFires

vars == <<holder, gen, expiry, clock, firedThisLease, totalFires>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
  /\ gen \in Nat
  /\ expiry \in Nat
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxTime
  /\ firedThisLease \in BOOLEAN
  /\ totalFires \in Nat

Init ==
  /\ holder = NoCar
  /\ gen = 0
  /\ expiry = 0
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ firedThisLease = FALSE
  /\ totalFires = 0

\* Acquiring the free bay starts a new lease generation and resets the
\* one-shot latch guarding the irreversible rinse/charge action.
AcquireLease(c) ==
  /\ holder = NoCar
  /\ holder' = c
  /\ gen' = gen + 1
  /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseLen
  /\ firedThisLease' = FALSE
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, totalFires>>

\* A slow-but-alive holder renews its own lease before expiry; this must
\* never start a new generation nor reset the fired latch.
Heartbeat(c) ==
  /\ holder = c
  /\ clock < expiry
  /\ expiry' = clock + LeaseLen
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, clock, firedThisLease, totalFires>>

\* The bay is only reclaimed once the lease has truly expired, i.e. no
\* heartbeat arrived in time -- a slow car that keeps heartbeating is safe.
ExpireLease ==
  /\ holder # NoCar
  /\ clock >= expiry
  /\ holder' = NoCar
  /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, expiry, clock, firedThisLease, totalFires>>

Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxTime
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, expiry, firedThisLease, totalFires>>

\* The current holder may trigger the irreversible rinse/charge action, but
\* only once per lease generation -- the latch blocks any repeat until the
\* bay is re-leased.
FireAction(c) ==
  /\ holder = c
  /\ ~firedThisLease
  /\ firedThisLease' = TRUE
  /\ totalFires' = totalFires + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, gen, expiry, clock>>

Next ==
  \/ ExpireLease
  \/ Tick
  \/ \E c \in Cars : AcquireLease(c) \/ Heartbeat(c) \/ FireAction(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Safety: the irreversible action can never have fired more times than
\* there have been lease generations -- at most once per lease/expiry cycle.

enter the bay and must hold the bay's lease before the final-rinse actuator
(which also fires the customer's payment charge) can trigger -- an
irreversible, one-shot action. The lease is granted with an expiry time; if
the current holder's clock runs out without renewal, the bay is reclaimed and
re-leased to a new generation, which resets the one-shot latch. A car can be

it keeps sending heartbeats before its lease's expiry, it is never treated as
failed and never loses the bay to another car mid-cycle. The mechanism must
guarantee that the irreversible rinse/charge action never fires more times
than there have been distinct lease generations, i.e. it cannot fire twice
within the same lease, and a slow-but-alive car cannot have its lease stolen
out from under it while it still occupies the bay.

---- MODULE W4Od9m4p1t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Feeders, MaxQ, MaxSeq

VARIABLES queue, record, nextSeq, crashed

vars == <<queue, record, nextSeq, crashed>>

\* The bounded work queue holds load-shed command tuples generated by
\* feeders; backpressure blocks new enqueues once the queue is full, and a
\* command already superseded by the shared record may be purged early to
\* free capacity without ever discarding a command that is still current.

InQueue(f, s) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i].feeder = f /\ queue[i].seq = s

TypeOK ==
  /\ queue \in Seq([feeder : Feeders, seq : 1..MaxSeq])
  /\ Len(queue) <= MaxQ
  /\ record \in [Feeders -> 0..MaxSeq]
  /\ nextSeq \in [Feeders -> 1..(MaxSeq + 1)]
  /\ crashed \subseteq Feeders

Init ==
  /\ queue = <<>>
  /\ record = [f \in Feeders |-> 0]
  /\ nextSeq = [f \in Feeders |-> 1]
  /\ crashed = {}

Enqueue(f) ==
  /\ f \notin crashed
  /\ nextSeq[f] <= MaxSeq
  /\ Len(queue) < MaxQ
  /\ queue' = Append(queue, [feeder |-> f, seq |-> nextSeq[f]])
  /\ nextSeq' = [nextSeq EXCEPT ![f] = @ + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, crashed>>

\* Apply always processes the head of the queue; a command only overwrites
\* the shared record if it is strictly newer, so a stale duplicate can never
\* clobber (lose) a fresher value already recorded.
Apply ==
  /\ queue # <<>>
  /\ LET cmd == Head(queue) IN
       /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
       /\ record' = IF cmd.seq > record[cmd.feeder]
                     THEN [record EXCEPT ![cmd.feeder] = cmd.seq]
                     ELSE record
  /\ UNCHANGED <<nextSeq, crashed>>

Crash(f) ==
  /\ f \notin crashed
  /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {f}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, record, nextSeq>>

\* Backpressure relief: drop a queued command only once it has already been
\* superseded by the shared record, freeing capacity without losing data.
ExpireStale ==
  /\ \E i \in DOMAIN queue :
       /\ queue[i].seq <= record[queue[i].feeder]
       /\ queue' = [j \in 1..(Len(queue) - 1) |-> IF j < i THEN queue[j] ELSE queue[j + 1]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, nextSeq, crashed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Enqueue(f)
  \/ Apply
  \/ \E f \in Feeders : Crash(f)
  \/ ExpireStale

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Apply)

\* Safety: commands for the same feeder never appear in the queue out of
\* generation order, so an older command can never be applied after (and
\* thus silently overwrite) a newer one -- no update to the shared record
\* is ever lost.
NoLostUpdates ==
  \A i \in DOMAIN queue : \A j \in DOMAIN queue :
    (i < j /\ queue[i].feeder = queue[j].feeder) => queue[i].seq < queue[j].seq

\* Liveness: every load-shed command placed in the queue by a feeder that
\* has not (yet) crashed is eventually reflected in the shared record.
EventuallyApplied ==
  \A f \in Feeders : \A s \in 1..MaxSeq :
    (InQueue(f, s) /\ f \notin crashed) ~> (record[f] >= s)

====

and applies them to one shared record of the last commanded setpoint per
feeder. Commands travel through a small bounded work queue: when the queue is
full, feeders experience backpressure and simply cannot enqueue a new command

producing new commands, without any cleanup or notification -- but any
commands it already queued must still be processed normally. The system must
never let backpressure relief or the silent crash cause a command to be lost
or applied out of order, and it must keep making progress on whatever is
still queued.

order they were generated, so an older command can never be applied after
(and thereby silently overwrite) a newer one already reflected in the shared
record.

TypeOK ==
  /\ holder \in Participants \cup {NoOne}
  /\ ticksLeft \in 0..LeaseLen
  /\ status \in [Participants -> {"alive", "crashed"}]
  /\ inCS \in [Participants -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ ticksLeft = 0
  /\ status = [p \in Participants |-> "alive"]
  /\ inCS = [p \in Participants |-> FALSE]

\* A live participant grabs the free match-commit lease and enters the critical section
Acquire(p) ==
  /\ holder = NoOne
  /\ status[p] = "alive"
  /\ holder' = p
  /\ ticksLeft' = LeaseLen
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED status

\* The holder commits the match and voluntarily releases the lease
Release(p) ==
  /\ holder = p
  /\ inCS[p]
  /\ status[p] = "alive"
  /\ holder' = NoOne
  /\ ticksLeft' = 0
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED status

\* The twist: the current holder crashes silently, the lease is left dangling
Crash(p) ==
  /\ holder = p
  /\ status[p] = "alive"
  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![p] = "crashed"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ticksLeft, inCS>>

\* Logical time advances while a lease is outstanding, counting down to expiry
Tick ==
  /\ holder # NoOne
  /\ ticksLeft > 0
  /\ ticksLeft' = ticksLeft - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, status, inCS>>

\* Expiry reclaims a timed-out lease, whether the holder crashed or is just slow

  /\ holder # NoOne
  /\ ticksLeft = 0
  /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![holder] = FALSE]
  /\ holder' = NoOne
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ticksLeft, status>>

Releasing == \E p \in Participants : Release(p)
Crashing  == \E p \in Participants : Crash(p)

             /\ WF_vars(Acquiring)
             /\ WF_vars(Releasing)
             /\ WF_vars(Tick)

nl:
In a multiplayer game lobby matchmaker, participants compete for a single
match-commit lease that guards the critical resource used to finalize a
match (only the lease holder may write the committed match result). A
participant acquires the free lease, enters the critical section, and
normally releases it once the match is committed. The twist: a lease
holder can crash silently, leaving the lease dangling with nobody able to
release it. To keep the system alive, every lease carries a bounded
countdown; once it hits zero the lease is forcibly expired and reclaimed,
regardless of whether the holder crashed or is merely slow, so another
live participant can acquire it later.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one participant is ever inside the match-commit
critical section at a time, and that participant is always the current
lease holder (never a stale or crashed one).
LIVENESS PROPERTY: The match-commit lease is infinitely often free, i.e.
even after its holder crashes silently the lease is always eventually
reclaimed via expiry and made available again.
